articles.title: JJ Gabriel: Manchester United case at heart of academy transfer market
articles.summary: BBC Sport explores why clubs at the top of English football are increasingly trading academy players and what the impact is on the youngsters themselves.
articles.body:
A 15-year-old growing up in the UK faces many tough personal decisions about their future - which school subjects to study, which social circle suits them, and where their priorities lie in life.

But in the past few weeks the choices teenage Manchester United striker JJ Gabriel has been making about his future in football have drawn huge public attention in sports media and online.

Gabriel has informed United he wants to leave the club and join another. BBC Sport has reported that he has stayed away from training and begun talking to other clubs because he and his representatives are unhappy with United's handling of the 15-year-old's progress.

That a transfer saga involving a footballer so young could generate so much interest highlights a truth that to many is uncomfortable - money is changing how the football transfer market works, and children are increasingly deemed to be among its most valuable commodities.

So what is behind the rise in transfers involving boys who in some cases are not even old enough to have taken their GCSEs, what kind of influence can the money on offer have on agents and parents, and what exactly are the country's top football clubs getting out of it?

"It's crazy when you think about it," says Ryan Cardwell, former youth scout at Liverpool and Southampton.

"In what other kind of world would 15 and 16-year-olds be spoken about in the media like this?"

This summer alone, all six of the Premier League's wealthiest clubs either signed a highly-rated academy player from another, or lost a youngster to a direct rival.

"It is such a competitive market," Cardwell explains. "There are now tens of transfers between the elite academies every summer, when it used to be the case that if you were already at one of those, you would likely stay the course.

"The race for talent is huge – you look at what teams are spending on transfers for senior players and it's enormous, so if you can spot a player earlier and offset some of that financial risk, you're going to do so."

Some inside football claim that the transfer of Rio Ngumoha - the now 18-year-old winger who was called up to this month's senior England squad - from Chelsea to Liverpool at the age of 15 in 2024 ushered in a new era of competition for academy players among the nation's elite.

One of the major factors is Brexit. Before 2021 English clubs were allowed to sign academy players over the age of 16 who held European Union passports.

Since the UK left the EU, foreign players cannot join English clubs until they reach 18.

"Heathrow and Gatwick [airports] on a Friday night were inundated with scouts going to other countries to look for young players", says Caldwell.

"Belgium and the Netherlands were full of scouts for Premier League clubs.

"Now it's the competition between English clubs that has increased, looking at each other's players, including the old-school 'top six' but also the likes of Southampton, Aston Villa , and Fulham ."

Young players have further added financial value - youth signings don't count towards the Premier League's squad cost ratio rules, and any future sale counts as 'pure profit' in club accounts.

Advances in video technology and data analysis mean more young players are being identified, tracked and approached by rival clubs than ever before.

'Money can mean agents or parents push a player to move'

Players can de-register from their academy at the end of their under-12, under-14 and under-16 seasons if they wish to explore options elsewhere.

They can be offered paid scholarship contracts from the season in which they turn 14, and can sign professional deals from the season in which they turn 16.

Some pundits and fans have criticised Gabriel's family over the controversy in recent weeks.

Gabriel can potentially join clubs in Europe because he has an Irish passport.

"It's a really tough world - players and families want the best for their kids and you can't give them stick without knowing what their motivations are," says Phil Jagielka, whose son Zac left Liverpool in 2024 and signed a scholarship deal at Hull City at 16.

"The harsh reality is that if a young player fails to progress, or gets a bad injury, teams will stop being interested in them. So there is an element of strike while the iron's hot."

When a club signs a player from a rival academy, they pay a set compensation fee based on how long they had been trained there.

Depending on the player's age, the fee can reach millions of pounds.

The increasing allure of signing young academy players from rivals means some parents are now compiling data packs on their sons to give to potential clubs, and more and more children are represented by football agents.

"There are good agents and bad agents," Cardwell says.

"You certainly speak to some and think 'that's completely the wrong idea', or, ' this player is going to be misguided'. Sometimes they push for a move when a player isn't ready.

"The contracts can be enormous and [money] can be a huge motivation to move. It could set a young player's family up for life.

"I would quite like to see some form of financial cap. My fear for some of the young players is they're on the biggest salaries they'll ever have, because if they don't make it at the top level, they can go from being on tens of thousands (of pounds) a week to one or two thousand lower down the pyramid."

'Far more people are prepared to rock the boat'

In decades gone by, development of academy players would be combined with menial tasks around the training ground.

The idea was to keep young footballers grounded and make them feel a part of the wider club.

But the Gabriel case demonstrates the significant changes football has undergone.

"We would clean boots, sweep floors, tidy the changing rooms," says Jagielka, who came through Sheffield United's academy in the late 1990s.

"I fully back that system. It taught us responsibility and discipline. It was a way of getting to know the first-team players, and you would get a proper telling off if you didn't do your jobs properly.

"There was nowhere near as much outside influence on young players back then. Now there is an entourage, people wanting to play the long game with, 9, 10, 11-year-olds because of the millions of pounds of commission if they turn out to be a superstar.

"There are far more people out there now who are prepared to rock the boat between the different clubs."

The public scrutiny on young players has increased significantly, and the elite clubs' desire to succeed in the market means that high-profile youth transfers involving big money seem to be here to stay.

"Young players now have such a big platform on social media that intrigue is part of day-to-day life for them," says Cardwell.

"When you're in elite sport you have to grow up really, really fast. Teenagers are expected to cope with the pressure and naturally some people fall into the trap of thinking 'well, he's a young man already' and forget about everything else.

"The race for talent is never, ever going to change."

articles.title: El impacto númerico de Miguel Sierra
articles.standfirst: El granadino, nominado a mejor sub-23 por segundo mes consecutivo, destaca en varias estadísticas de LaLiga
articles.summary: El granadino, nominado a mejor sub-23 por segundo mes consecutivo, destaca en varias estadísticas de LaLiga
articles.body: Miguel Sierra está dejando de ser una sorpresa para convertirse en realidad. En las siete primeras jornadas de LaLiga, el extremo derecho del Sevilla se ha erigido en la pieza más determinante para el ataque hispalense. Tanto es así que ha sido nominado a mejor jugador sub-23 por segundo mes consecutivo, un premio por el que esta vez competirá con Pau Cubarsí (Barcelona), Alberto Moleiro (Villarreal), Yassir Zabiri (Racing) y Yoel Lago (Celta). Una irrupción en el fútbol profesional que viene avalada por un impacto numérico notable, confirmando que el granadino ha llegado al primer equipo para quedarse. A sus 22 años, Sierra es indispensable en los planes de Luis García Plaza. Si ya en pretemporada el entrenador madrileño apostó por darle bastante protagonismo, posteriormente lo ha incluido en el once inicial en los siete partidos que ha disputado el Sevilla. De hecho, después de los cuatro futbolistas que lo han jugado todo (Vlachodimos, Suazo, Juan Iglesias y Agoumé), el atacante zurdo es el que más ha participado hasta la fecha con 491 minutos. Además, ha anotado dos goles que lo colocan al frente de la producción ofensiva junto con Isaac Romero. "El año pasado se asentaron canteranos conmigo en la alineación titular. Miguel está aprovechando su momento y su oportunidad. Siempre digo que intento ser justo con todos. Está ganándose su sitio y no se lo voy a quitar hasta que no rinda. Si sigue siendo así, pues seguirá siendo titular", aseguró García Plaza tras el triunfo de los suyos en Riazor. Aquel choque se decidió gracias a un tanto marcado por el propio Sierra, que completó una actuación histórica como sevillista: más de 10 recuperaciones, 10 regates y 10 duelos en un mismo partido liguero, algo que no sucedía desde la temporada 2005-06. Una de las principales amenazas ofensivas del Sevilla reside en la verticalidad de Miguel Sierra. Según los datos de OptaAnalyst, con el balón en los pies lidera al equipo en carreras realizadas (75), en distancia total recorrida (942,5 metros) y en metros por carrera (12,6). En cuanto regates, destaca incluso como uno de los mejores de toda la Primera División (18), únicamente por detrás de nombres ilustres como Lamine Yamal (30), Kylian Mbappé (25) y Jude Bellingham (20). De cara a la portería rival, Sierra es el futbolista del Sevilla que ha intentado un mayor número de disparos (10) y el que más veces lo ha hecho entre los tres palos (5). Asimismo, si excluimos las jugadas a balón parado, sobresale como el que ha dado más pases clave que terminan en ocasión de gol (6); en este sentido, el extremo granadino promedia 2,36 centros al área por cada 90 minutos, el segundo registro más alto en el conjunto blanquirrojo después de Juan Iglesias (2,86). Más allá de su talento ofensivo, el compromiso y el esfuerzo de Miguel Sierra también se reflejan en su radiografía estadística, que lo aúpa a la élite de LaLiga en el apartado de las disputas. Y es que se trata del segundo jugador de todo el campeonato que ha ganado más duelos terrestres (44), igualado con Lamine Yamal y solamente superado por Jude Bellingham (49). Este dato se refuerza teniendo en cuenta su enorme implicación en la resta, ya que se sitúa entre los seis futbolistas de ataque con más entradas tanto exitosas (8) como intentadas (12). Es evidente que el gran nivel mostrado por Sierra es uno de los motivos que explican el buen arranque del Sevilla. En este momento el granadino es, sin ninguna duda, el extremo que ofrece mejor rendimiento en ambos lados de la cancha, lo que le ha servido para granjearse la confianza de Luis García Plaza y adueñarse de la banda derecha. Por tanto, ni siquiera el regreso de Rubén Vargas debería alterar su estatus en la plantilla. En Nervión han encontrado una nueva perla con la que ilusionarse.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal y las críticas por 'reclamar' el Balón de Oro: "La gente pide cosas que luego no quiere"
articles.standfirst: El jugador del Barça volvió a hablar del galardón que se entrega en octubre
articles.summary: El jugador del Barça volvió a hablar del galardón que se entrega en octubre
articles.body: Lamine Yamal sigue insistiendo en que se merece el Balón de Oro y así lo contó a Teledeporte en una entrevista. El internacional español considera que este año tiene más opciones que en la pasada edición, en buena medida por la posibilidad de conquistar el Mundial con España: "Tengo más posibilidades que el año pasado. Me faltó la Champions, que la ganó el PSG, pero este año tenemos el Mundial". El jugador del Barcelona sabe que la decisión no depende de él, pero se muestra satisfecho con la temporada que ha realizado y con su rendimiento: "Las posibilidades están ahí. El juego ha estado, todo ha estado… pero no depende de mí. Estoy tranquilo con lo que he hecho". Lamine vuelve así a defender públicamente sus opciones a un premio que ya estuvo cerca de conquistar el pasado año, quedando segundo por detrás de Dembélé. El extremo también reivindica una forma de jugar que, según él, debe tener peso en la elección del ganador. "En el fútbol europeo hay pocos jugadores que jueguen como yo lo hago y que hagan disfrutar a la gente de esta manera. Es mi objetivo, siempre lo he dicho. Mi referente era Neymar por eso”, cuenta. Una filosofía que relaciona directamente con lo que, a su juicio, debe premiar el Balón de Oro: “El Balón de Oro tiene que ver con eso, con jugadores que están un poco por encima”. Lamine es consciente de que sus declaraciones sobre el premio generan debate, pero asegura que no piensa cambiar su manera de expresarse: “Piden que los futbolistas sean sinceros, luego digo lo que pienso… y dicen ‘pero cómo va a decir eso’. La gente pide cosas que luego no quiere. No voy a cambiar mi forma de ser hasta que me retire ni voy a decir algo que no pienso”. Y, aunque defiende sus propias opciones, también tuvo palabras para uno de sus compañeros y dejó claro quién sería su elección para el galardón destinado al mejor joven: “Le daría a Cubarsí el Balón de Oro joven”.

articles.title: Israel’s Abu Farchi sent off for gun celebration in Nations League match
articles.summary: Israel footballer Sayed Abu Farchi was sent off for goal celebration mimicking shooting a gun in match against Austria.
articles.body:
Israel footballer Sayed Abu Farchi was sent off for his goal-scoring celebration when he used the corner flag ⁠to simulate a gun after equalizing against Austria in their UEFA Nations League late on Thursday.

The forward’s goal levelled the match 1-1 early in the second half at Raiffeisen Arena in Linz, Austria, his 55th minute header cancelling out Romano Schmid’s first-half penalty.

The 20-year-old then jogged to the corner, pulled out the corner flag, dropped his right knee to the grass and rested the pole on the back of his left hand before making a firing gesture.

It wasn’t immediately clear if Farchi, who plays his club football in Major League Soccer (MLS) in the United States, was about to simulate a pool cue shot or a weapon, but the action that followed left no one in doubt.

The referee promptly showed the Colorado Rapids forward a second yellow card, just four minutes after his first, leading to a red card.

Under the International Football Association Board Law 12, players can celebrate a goal as they wish, but their celebration “must not be excessive” and a player “must be cautioned for acting in a provocative, derisory or inflammatory way”.

Austria regained ⁠the lead in the 90th minute through Phillipp Mwene, who netted following a cross from ‌Paul Wanner. Sasa Kalajdzic added a third goal in stoppage time with a ‌close-range ‌finish to seal a 3-1 win.

Israel’s participation in the Nations League has prompted fierce backlash from several other competing countries, including the Republic of Ireland, whose football association said its request to avoid future pairings with Israel had been ⁠⁠ rejected by UEFA .

A banner with the words “Free Palestine” was also displayed by Austrian fans close to the pitch during Thursday’s match.

Ireland face Israel on Sunday in a match to be hosted at a neutral venue – Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen, Hungary – before hosting the return fixture on October 4.

Al Jazeera has contacted UEFA and Colorado Rapids for a response to Farchi’s celebratory simulation.

articles.title: Despiden a un entrenador en Valladolid por mensajes racistas contra marroquíes y sudamericanos

articles.summary: El hombre pertenecía al Club Deportivo Juventud Rondilla que tras tener conocimiento de estos mensajes ha despedido rápidamente al entrenador.
articles.body: El Club Deportivo Juventud Rondilla ha informado este jueves, a través de sus redes sociales, de que ha rescindido el acuerdo que mantenía con uno de sus nuevos entrenadores por sus comentarios "racistas y xenófobos" vertidos en redes sociales y en los que emplea términos "explícitamente despectivos hacia la población marroquí y sudamericana". Tras tener conocimiento de estos hechos, la Junta Directiva del Club se ha reunido de "urgencia" y, ante "la extrema gravedad de las manifestaciones realizadas" por el entrenador, se ha acordado por unanimidad rescindir de forma inmediata el acuerdo que unía a ambas partes. Asimismo, el C.D Juventud Rondilla considera que los comentarios del entrenador "constituyen una falta muy grave" y recuerda que la Rondilla es un barrio "diverso, multicultural y acogedor" y la comunidad marroquí y sudamericana "forman parte fundamental del barrio y de la gran familia" que es el club. En esta línea, el Club ha añadido que como entidad dedicada a la educación y formación de menores, tiene el deber de "velar por un entorno seguro, integrador y basado en el respeto mutuo" a lo que añade que no va a tolerar que personas que difunden "discursos de odio o discriminación" estén a cargo de la formación de los niños.

articles.title: Polémico debut de Xavi Hernández como seleccionador de Países Bajos por "un gol antideportivo"
articles.standfirst: Rafael van der Vaart, ex del Madrid, denuncia la anulación de un gol de Países Bajos y la actitud antideportiva de Alemania en su 1-0
articles.summary: Rafael van der Vaart, ex del Madrid, denuncia la anulación de un gol de Países Bajos y la actitud antideportiva de Alemania en su 1-0
articles.body: Xavi Hernández tuvo un polémico debut como seleccionador de Países Bajos en el partido que acabó empatando 1-1 contra Alemania en la Nations League. Rafael van der Vaart, ex de Real Madrid y Betis, se quejó por la decisión del árbitro español Alejandro Hernández Hernández de anular un gol que hubiese supuesto el 1-0 para Países Bajos en el estadio Johan Cruyff Arena de Ámsterdam. En el minuto 13 Virgil van Dijk remató de cabeza al fondo de la red de Marc-André ter Stegen en un saque de córner, pero Hernández Hernández anuló el gol tras la revisión del VAR de Carlos del Cerro por una obstaculización de Brobbey al portero de Alemania. "¡Es una vergüenza! Increíble. Brobbey apenas hizo nada. Seguro que se le puede tocar. El portero no puede hacer lo que quiera", denunció Van der Vaart en el canal de televisión NOS. Van der Vaart no dudó en criticar la actuación de ter Stegen: "Fue una actuación floja. Creo que hoy está jugando mal en general. Sobre todo con los pies, que normalmente es su punto fuerte. Pero esa es otra historia. El gol nunca debió haber sido anulado". El otra gran polémica se produjo con el gol de Alemania, con el que Félix Nmecha puso el 1-0 después de que el delantero neerlandés Brobbey cayese al suelo sin contacto alguno. El equipo alemán no detuvo el partido, siguió con la jugada y acabó marcando. "Es duro para Brobbey, pero lo que me parece realmente grave es que dejaron de jugar. Amiri simula que va a echar el balón del campo y luego se detiene. Como resultado, todos dejan de jugar... Creo que los holandeses estaban despistados. Obviamente, eso es antideportivo, pero hay algo en juego, ¿no? Son las reglas", explicó Rafael van der Vaart. Xavi Hernández se mostró "satisfecho" con el juego de Países Bajos en su estreno como seleccionador, en especial en una segunda mitad en la que, defendió, los neerlandeses mostraron "la personalidad" y la "ambición" que él quiere implantar a los jugadores. "Estoy satisfecho porque jugamos muy bien. Creo que, sinceramente, fuimos mejores que Alemania... En la primera parte quizá estuvimos un poco nerviosos, pero la manera en la que jugamos en la segunda parte es la correcta", aseguró Xavi rueda de prensa. Xavi destacó la respuesta de su equipo después del descanso, cuando se encontraba por detrás en el marcador: "Mostramos personalidad, ambición, deseo de ganar y una buena intensidad. Lo que más me gustó fue, definitivamente, la personalidad en la segunda parte cuando íbamos perdiendo, la actitud de los jugadores y la mentalidad". El técnico español subrayó también la voluntad de dominar el balón como elementos del "nuevo" equipo neerlandés.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership crowds break four million mark
articles.summary: Scottish Premiership crowds topped four million for the first time last season as the league continues to attract the highest per capita attendances in Europe.
articles.body:
Scottish Premiership crowds topped four million for the first time last season as the league continues to attract the highest per capita attendances in Europe.

From a 4.1m total, average gates in the top flight reached 17,903, up by 3%, as Celtic defended their title thanks to a dramatic final-day victory at home to challengers Hearts.

Only England, Germany, Spain, Italy, France and the Netherlands attracted bigger audiences overall.

Adjusting average crowds for population puts Scotland way out in front with close to 20 attendees per 1,000 residents, nearly twice the figure for the next best nation, Norway.

Figures published by Uefa show approximately six million Scottish supporters watched men's matches during the 2025-26 campaign, with 900,000 in the lower leagues, 200,000 at domestic cup ties and 800,000 at European matches.

Champions Celtic were the only club outside Europe's big five leagues to exceed one million for home Premiership crowds.

Across all competitions, Rangers broke the one million mark.

The reports also shows just over two-thirds of all Premiership minutes last season were played by non-Scots.

The European average is 47%, with only Greece, Portugal and Turkey having a lower percentage of locally trained talent than Scotland.

Norway, Spain, Czech Republic, Netherlands and Sweden were the nations with figures above 60%.

The Scottish FA have submitted proposals to increase playing time for young players , with SPFL clubs to vote on the matter in November.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s Konate suffers injury ahead of Roma match
articles.summary: Anticipation is growing among Roma fans for José Mourinho’s return to the Olimpico, scheduled for October 14th. The Giallorossi will face Real Madrid on that...
articles.body:
Anticipation is growing among Roma fans for José Mourinho's return to the Olimpico, scheduled for October 14th.

The Giallorossi will face Real Madrid on that date in the second matchday of the Champions League.

However, there is bad news for the Portuguese coach. Ibrahima Konaté is also a doubt for the match against his former teammate.

The rock-solid defender, who arrived on a free transfer in the summer, had established himself as a starting defender for the Madrid club, but he could be sidelined against Roma.

Yesterday, the Frenchman underwent tests, which revealed a torn collateral ligament in his right leg.

Konaté's recovery time remains to be determined: his condition will be monitored by Real Madrid's staff on a daily basis. If he misses out, it would be bad news for Mourinho, who still doesn't know if Federico Valverde will be available.

The long layoff, in this case, is doing the Blancos a favor. The Special One hopes to have both players fit for the match against Roma, but he won't be caught off guard. Eduardo Camavinga will warm up in place of the Uruguayan, while Antonio Rudiger , another former star, could find space in defense.

articles.title: Report: Chelsea favourites to sign Premier League midfielder
articles.summary: Chelsea Interest in Alex Scott Could Become Major Transfer StoryChelsea’s midfield search is already beginning to take shape, and while Lamine Camara continu...
articles.body:
Chelsea Interest in Alex Scott Could Become Major Transfer Story

Chelsea's midfield search is already beginning to take shape, and while Lamine Camara continues to generate plenty of attention, Alex Scott might ultimately become the more intriguing name to watch.

The Daily Mail reports that Chelsea regard the Bournemouth midfielder as a top target, although securing him during the January transfer window could prove extremely difficult.

That should surprise nobody. Scott is becoming increasingly important to Bournemouth and, at 23, fits neatly into the profile Chelsea have repeatedly targeted.

The Daily Mail makes Bournemouth's position particularly clear:

"Chelsea regarding Alex Scott as a top target is no secret, though Bournemouth categorically insisted they would not do a deal in the summer and they may stand by that stance this January, too. Convincing another club to part with one of their better players midway through a campaign can be extremely challenging, and costly."

Bournemouth have little incentive to make life easy for Chelsea. Scott is under contract, is established in the Premier League and has developed into a midfielder capable of influencing games through possession, movement and intelligent positioning.

Any January negotiation would therefore begin from a position of considerable Bournemouth strength.

There is also recent evidence of how Bournemouth approach valuable assets.

"Bournemouth sold Antoine Semenyo to Manchester City last January but that was via his release clause worth £65m. When Bournemouth eventually warm towards selling Scott, we can expect Chelsea to be at the table."

Scott presents a different situation if there is no contractual mechanism forcing Bournemouth into negotiations.

That potentially leaves Chelsea facing a simple question. How much extra are they prepared to pay for January availability?

Mid season transfers involving important Premier League players tend to carry a premium because the selling club must consider the sporting consequences alongside the financial return.

Camara Competition Adds Another Dimension

Chelsea's wider midfield search also includes Monaco 's Lamine Camara, whose proposed £47million move collapsed on deadline day.

Camara remains admired at Stamford Bridge, although Monaco's excellent start and Liverpool 's reported interest could complicate matters considerably.

That makes Scott particularly interesting. Chelsea already know the Premier League player, they have maintained their admiration and Bournemouth know that interest exists.

There is no obvious reason for Bournemouth to rush.

Scott's performances can strengthen their negotiating position further, while Chelsea must decide whether January urgency outweighs the financial advantages of waiting until summer.

For Scott, meanwhile, continued development at Bournemouth could make that eventual decision considerably bigger. Chelsea may already be watching closely, but they are unlikely to be alone for long.

From a Chelsea supporter's perspective, Alex Scott is probably the name here that deserves particularly close attention.

There is something appealing about targeting a 23 year old midfielder who already understands Premier League football. Chelsea have invested heavily in potential, and Scott offers potential alongside meaningful experience of the division.

Bournemouth have absolutely no reason to sell cheaply. If Scott remains an important player and there is no release clause creating an obvious route into negotiations, Chelsea could be quoted an enormous figure simply because Bournemouth can afford to say no.

That should encourage patience rather than panic.

Camara is clearly an attractive alternative, although Liverpool's reported interest and Monaco's position make that deal complicated too. Chelsea therefore appear to be looking at midfielders who are young enough to develop while already possessing substantial first team experience.

Scott fits that description beautifully.

If Bournemouth eventually indicate that they are prepared to negotiate, Chelsea should certainly be part of that conversation. Until then, watching how Scott develops this season might tell us whether he can become the type of midfielder worth making a major investment in.

January could come too soon. The longer term interest feels far more significant.

articles.title: UK Football Police Unit accused of ‘bringing Hillsborough’ into alcohol debate
articles.summary: A spokesperson for the UK Football Policing Unit ‘it was not our intention to link the issue of alcohol with the Hillsborough tragedy’
articles.body:
English football's leading fans' group has criticised the UK Football Policing Unit for "bringing Hillsborough into the debate" around drinking in sight of the pitch.

The topic of changing the law to allow fans to drink at their seat or in the stands has resurfaced after Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the rules were outdated and discriminatory and should be scrapped.

The Football Supporters' Association (FSA) immediately backed his call but the UKFPU urged caution, stating: "Following a number of football-related tragedies, changes in legislation were implemented after the Taylor Report for good reason and we are currently in the longest ever period without a significant football-related disaster.

"The UKFPU added it would be "incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence".

The Taylor Report referenced by the UKFPU was commissioned in the wake of the 1989 Hillsborough disaster, which resulted in the deaths of 97 Liverpool fans.

The FSA published a thread on its X account setting out its position on drinking in the stands which began: "Arguably the most important point is that the UK Football Policing Unit's comments bringing Hillsborough into this debate have to be corrected. The disaster was not caused by alcohol. Full stop.

"Fans were 'unlawfully killed and a catalogue of failings by police and the ambulance services contributed to their deaths'."

A spokesperson for the UKFPU said: "It was not our intention to link the issue of alcohol with the Hillsborough tragedy. The laws around alcohol, which we acknowledge were first introduced in 1985, are one of a range of measures in addition to the subsequent Taylor Report recommendations that have contributed to making football much safer for fans in this country."

Burnham's comments have sparked a social media debate on the topic , where differing views have been expressed by match-going fans.

The FSA's post on Thursday added: "It's unfair to criminalise fans for having a pint – especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league."We are fundamentally sceptical of any law which is only targeted at football supporters.

"That doesn't mean every club should be forced to serve alcohol to every seat! A club should have the choice to do what is right for its fans. Consultation is critical, some stadiums or stands might not be suitable (e.g. family areas) whereas it might be popular elsewhere.

"Ultimately, we think clubs, in liaison with their supporters, should be able to determine what is best for themselves, rather than relying on legislation which is decades old and was written through the prism of viewing all football fans as potential hooligans."

The Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol) Act 1985 prohibits drinking in sight of the pitch in England and Wales in the top five men's leagues.

Burnham said on Wednesday: "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point.

"I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.

"And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis.

"But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long-held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently from others."

articles.title: Israel striker sent off for gun celebration in Nations League defeat to Austria
articles.summary: Saied Abu Farchi was shown a second yellow card during the 3-1 loss to Austria after using the corner flag to simulate a gun during his goal celebration
articles.body:
Israel forward ​Saied Abu Farchi was sent off for celebrating his goal against Austria in their 3-1 ⁠ Nations League defeat by using the corner flag to simulate a gun.

Abu Farchi headed home in the 55th minute to bring Israel level after Austria had taken the lead through a Romano Schmid penalty before half-time at the Raiffeisen Arena in Linz.

The 20-year-old ran to the ‌corner flag, grabbed it ‌and made a gun-firing gesture during his celebration.

The referee had booked Abu Farchi four minutes earlier and showed him a second yellow card for the celebration, followed by a red, leaving Israel with 10 players for the remainder of the match.

Austria regained the lead in ‌the 90th minute through Phillipp ​ Mwene , who netted following ‌a cross from ⁠Paul Wanner and Sasa Kalajdzic added ⁠a third in stoppage time with ‌a close-range ​finish to seal victory.

Israel next face Republic of Ireland on Sunday evening in a match where the build-up has been steeped in controversy .

The Israeli FA accused Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson of "hypocrisy and stupidity" after he said his team would be "playing against genocide" in the upcoming double header between the two teams, which will be taking place in neutral venues in Hungary and Serbia due to safety concerns.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) have confirmed that they will fulfill both fixtures despite mounting calls from campaigners to boycott the games but after announcing his squad, Hallgrimsson admitted that "none of us feel comfortable playing in these games".

When asked how his players can focus on the fixtures given the calls to boycott the games back home, Hallgrimsson added: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

In a furious response on social media, the Israeli FA wrote: "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way. Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

The Irish taoiseach Michael Martin called the comments from the Israeli FA "unacceptable" and said they "should be withdrawn" while speaking with reporters when attending the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

The Israeli government has vehemently denied the charges of genocide since their retaliation to the October 7 attacks almost three years ago, when about 1,200 people were killed by Hamas and 250 people were taken hostage. Over 70,000 Palestinians have since been killed in the war in Gaza, according to figures used by the United Nations.

In the pre-match press conference for their Nations League clash with Kosovo on Thursday – which Ireland ultimately lost 1-0 – Hallgrimsson then acknowledged that his comments had not necessarily been the smartest move.

"Creating the headlines from what I said last time has taken the attention away from what is maybe most important, we are playing an important game against Kosovo," said the Icelandic coach.

"That was not the purpose and maybe from a leadership point of view it was not clever from me, to take the attention like this. I need to be focused on the game need and the players need to be focused on the game. To answer the question, we're thankful for the support we get. It's a tricky time for us."

Meanwhile, captain Dara O'Shea said the Irish players will come together and discuss whether to stage a protest before playing Israel, with a decision to be taken by the squad "as one".

O'Shea said the Irish team have been put in a "difficult" and "unusual" situation ahead of the games against Israel and will make a decision on what to do ahead of the weekend.

articles.title: COPE journalist fires back at Florentino Perez after Real Madrid’s attack: ‘Their problem is that Barça are six points ahead’
articles.summary: Juanma Castano has hit back at Real Madrid after the club published a video compiling comments he has made over the past decade, escalating an already tense...
articles.body:
Juanma Castano has hit back at Real Madrid after the club published a video compiling comments he has made over the past decade, escalating an already tense dispute between the COPE journalist and the Spanish giants.

The latest exchange follows Castano's apology for comparing Real Madrid TV with the newspaper Gara in an ABC column.

Real Madrid had described that comparison as "an extremely serious act that crosses all boundaries" and reserved the right to take further measures.

The club then published a video featuring clips of Castano and his programme, prompting the journalist to respond on El Partidazo de COPE .

Castano accuses Florentino of continuing his campaign

Addressing the latest video , Castano directly linked the decision to Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and argued that their long-running disagreement had entered a new phase.

"Florentino Perez is continuing the crusade he's waged against me. Today he's made a video compiling moments of me and the 'Partidazo' over the last 10 years.

"They've cut it, edited it, added this and that – I don't know what. And they've uploaded it.

"As Florentino isn't on social media, he's uploaded it directly to Real Madrid's social media accounts, which is something completely unprecedented. I don't think it's ever happened before."

Castano then explained why he believes the latest intervention shows the president's view of him as an opponent, while making clear that he has no intention of changing how he operates.

"I am very surprised at how low Florentino has stooped in his treatment of his enemies".

The journalist then argued that his refusal to tailor his opinions to what he believes the Madrid president wants is at the heart of their dispute.

"I'm not going to say whatever Florentino Perez wants me to say here. And that's what Florentino finds hardest to bear.

"That I've never adapted to the style of radio that he surely wants. He's turned me into an enemy. And I believe that the enemies are elsewhere," he stressed.

Castano says Real Madrid's problem is Barcelona

Castano also shifted the discussion towards the current footballing situation, arguing that his criticism should not be confused with Real Madrid's performances on the pitch.

"I'm not Real Madrid's problem. Real Madrid's problem is that Barça are six points ahead and play excellent football. And I've got nothing to do with that.

"I won't threaten or intimidate people by slinging a load of rubbish at them. I'm not going to change. I'm going to carry on like this," he noted.

He then expanded on his view of the latest confrontation, contrasting his current relationship with Perez with the more prominent figures he says the president previously opposed.

"The first thing I want to say is that I'm very surprised – very surprised – at how Florentino has lowered the bar when it comes to his enemies.

"I mean, Florentino used to have Ceferin, the UEFA president, and Sánchez Galán, the chairman of Iberdrola, as his enemies, and now, all of a sudden, he's taken me and 'El Partidazo' on as his enemies.

"And he's going all out. And that's something which, perhaps, also shows a certain weakness."

Castano ultimately finished by insisting that the dispute would not alter his approach to his work.

"I'm not going to change. I'm going to stay the same."

articles.title: Ter Stegen brands Barcelona ‘unstoppable’ under Hansi Flick: ‘I wish them all the best from afar’
articles.summary: Marc-Andre ter Stegen has offered a strong endorsement of Hansi Flick’s work at Barcelona, describing the Blaugrana as “unstoppable” while continuing his own...
articles.body:
Marc-Andre ter Stegen has offered a strong endorsement of Hansi Flick's work at Barcelona , describing the Blaugrana as "unstoppable" while continuing his own comeback with Ajax.

The German goalkeeper returned to international duty after several months away and started for Germany in their 1-1 draw against the Netherlands.

It was a significant step for the Barcelona loanee after a difficult period, with the 33-year-old clearly pleased to be back representing his country.

His focus may now be on Ajax, but his connection with Barcelona remains strong.

Ter Stegen reflects on his return with Germany

Ter Stegen's return to the Germany starting XI carried particular importance given everything he has experienced over recent years.

Ter Stegen returned to international duty with Germany. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

The goalkeeper admitted that just being back on the pitch for his country was something he valued greatly.

"I felt good. I'm proud of the journey I've been on and everything I've given, given what I've been through in recent years, and now I'm just very happy to be back here," he explained.

The former Barcelona captain also made clear that returning to the international setup has not changed his competitive ambitions.

Simply put, Ter Stegen still wants to establish himself as Germany's first-choice goalkeeper and believes performances like the one against the Netherlands can help him achieve that.

"My aim is always to be number one. To be 100% fit and up to the task. And today was a good opportunity to prove that once again," he said.

Ter Stegen has praised Hansi Flick's Barcelona. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

Despite being away from Barcelona on loan , Ter Stegen continues to follow developments at his former club closely. Asked about Barça's impressive start under Flick, the goalkeeper had an emphatic response.

"They're unstoppable right now, and that's what I wish for them because they're working hard with Hansi as their manager, and I obviously wish them all the best from afar.

"But I'm at another club and focused on my own business.

"That said, I'm always keeping an eye on what they're doing, and I'm really happy for them that things are going so well," he concluded.

articles.title: ‘In my head, I knew I was leaving’ – Raphinha reveals how Hansi Flick convinced him to stay at Barcelona

articles.title: Lane Kiffin's Year 1 records: Inside LSU coach's struggles in first seasons at Tennessee, Ole Miss & more
articles.summary: A look back at how Kiffin has failed to win big during his first seasons as a head coach.
articles.body:
LSU head coach Lane Kiffin was hired as the Tigers' next head coach to fill some big expectations. His predecessor, Brian Kelly, was fired midseason after failing to get the Tigers to the College Football Playoff after four seasons.

Kiffin had led Ole Miss to its first-ever CFP last season, although he left before getting to coach his team through it. Armed with seemingly unlimited NIL resources, including a reported $40 million roster, LSU's playoff chances took a hit with last week's 32-24 loss to Ole Miss.

While LSU is still very much in the hunt for the CFP, the loss might be the first sign that Kiffin will have a down first season in Baton Rouge. In fact, Kiffin historically throughout his career has had poor first seasons as a first-year head coach. The trend even dates back to his time with the Oakland Raiders in 2007, and as recently as his first season with Ole Miss in 2020. MORE: What did Al Davis say about Lane Kiffin? Revisiting messy 2007 firing from Raiders

Despite having zero NFL experience, Raiders owner Al Davis signed Kiffin to a two-year $2 million contract. At the time of his hiring at 31 years old, he was both the youngest head coach in Raiders franchise history.

Kiffin's tenure was defined by his rocky relationship with Davis. Ahead of the 2007 NFL Draft, Kiffin apparently begged Davis to select receiver Calvin Johnson . Davis picked quarterback JaMarcus Russell instead. Russell bombed as a raider and is still widely regarded as one of the biggest busts in NFL history.

Russell even held out of training camp and the start of Oakland's season in 2007 due to contract negotiations with the team. Kiffin started Josh McCown instead, and Oakland lost 36-21 in Week 1.

The Raiders lost 23-20 on the road against Denver in Week 2 and defeated the Cleveland Browns and Miami Dolphins to reach 2-2 after Week 4. But Oakland proceeded to lose 10 out of its final 12 games, finishing 4-12 on the season.

According to ESPN's Chris Mortensen, Davis reportedly asked Kiffin to resign after his first season in Oakland. Kiffin reportedly refused. The Raiders ultimately denied the report. MORE: Meet the 20-year-old Ole Miss student behind viral Lane Kiffin taunting photo

His first and only season at Tennessee was actually one of his most successful. After getting fired by the Raiders just four weeks into the 2008 season, he returned to college football ahead of the 2009 season.

In Knoxville, he was tasked to replace longtime Vols head coach Philip Fulmer, who won a national championship at Tennessee in 1998.

Led by quarterback Jonathan Crompton and running back Montario Hardesty, the Vols finished the regular season 7-5, with SEC East wins over Georgia, No. 21 South Carolina and Vanderbilt. But Tennessee struggled against most ranked teams it faced, losing to No. 1s Florida and Alabama, as well as losses to UCLA and Ole Miss.

The Vols fell 37-14 to No. 12 Virginia Tech in the Chick-Fil-A Bowl.

Kiffin shockingly left Tennessee after his lone season there, calling USC his "dream job." He had previously worked for several seasons under Pete Carroll with the Trojans from 2001-2006.

Before the season even began, the NCAA hit Kiffin's new team with a bowl ban, as well as numerous scholarship reductions stemming from the Reggie Bush improper benefits scandal under Carroll.

Led by quarterback Matt Barkley , running back Marc Tyler and receivers Robert Woods and Ronald Johnson, the Trojans won anyway. USC got out to a 4-0 start, defeating Hawaii on the road, Virginia, and beating Minnesota and Washington State away from home.

The Trojans went 1-3 in October, falling to fWashington, No. 16 Stanford and No. 1 Oregon. USC finished the regular season with a 2-2 mark, beating Arizona State and No. 18 Arizona, before dropping its last two games to Oregon State and Notre Dame, but closed out the season beating rival UCLA 28-14 to finish 7-5.

Kiffin had to rebuild his coaching reputation at Alabama, spending three seasons on Nick Saban's staff in Tuscaloosa. During his first season at Florida Atlantic, the Owls got off to a 1-3 start, with losses to Navy, as well as road losses vs. No. 9 Wisconsin and Buffalo.

But FAU rattled off 10 straight wins from there, and clinched a trip to the first-ever C-USA title game in school history. The Owls also reached 11 wins for the very first time in program history .

Kiffin coached the Owls in the Boca Raton Bowl, beating Akron 50-3.

After compiling a 26-13 record at FAU, he was hired to take over at Ole Miss in Dec. 2019.

Kiffin's first year in Oxford came during a shortened season in 2020. College football's COVID season was a weird one for teams across the country, as teams and coaches played through positive tests and quarantines.

Ole Miss started the season 1-4, with losses to No. 5 Florida, No. 2 Alabama, Arkansas and Auburn. But the Rebels rattled off three wins over Vanderbilt, South Carolina and Mississippi State. Due to COVID rescheduling, Ole Miss played its final game of the regular season on Dec. 19, losing to LSU in Baton Rouge 53-48. LSU defeated Indiana in the Outback Bowl 26-20.

Of course, even after LSU's road loss to Ole Miss, the Tigers are still very much in the CFP hunt. This week, LSU faces No. 23 Texas A&M at home before facing a remaining ranked opponent in No. 24 Mississippi State on Oct. 17. LSU's month of November looks particularly tough, featuring games against No. 8 Alabama, No. 1 Texas and a road trip to No. 14 Tennessee on Nov. 21.

Kiffin was hired to lead LSU to the CFP as early as this season, and anything less than that would be considered a failure.

articles.title: De Ketelaere: "Hablé con el PSG, pero finalmente eligieron a Ferran Torres"
articles.standfirst: "Se hablaba de una cantidad cercana a los 50 millons. Pero hace falta encontrar un equipo dispuesto a pagarla"
articles.summary: "Se hablaba de una cantidad cercana a los 50 millons. Pero hace falta encontrar un equipo dispuesto a pagarla"
articles.body: El internacional belga Charles De Ketelaere, jugador del Atalanta, reveló que mantuvo conversaciones con el París Saint-Germain (PSG) este verano, aunque el club francés terminó decantándose por el español Ferran Torres, hasta entonces futbolista del Barcelona. "Hablé con el PSG, pero finalmente eligieron a Ferran Torres", explicó De Ketelaere, de 25 años, en una entrevista con el diario DH Les Sports en la que abordó las opciones que tuvo de abandonar el conjunto italiano. Preguntado por si la dirección del Atalanta no estaba dispuesta a dejarle marchar por menos de unos 50 millones de euros, el atacante belga respondió que esa cifra se aproximaba a las pretensiones del club. "Sí, creo que se hablaba de una cantidad cercana a esa. Pero hace falta encontrar un equipo dispuesto a pagarla. En la Premier League hay varios clubes que pueden hacerlo, pero al final no se concretó nada", señaló el atacante, que continuará esta temporada en el equipo italiano. De Ketelaere aseguró, en cualquier caso, que está satisfecho con su situación en Bérgamo y recordó que su temporada en el Milan, en la campaña 2022-23, le hizo valorar especialmente la importancia de disponer de minutos con regularidad. "Estoy contento en el Atalanta. Sé lo importante que es ser titular después de mi experiencia en el AC Milan. Algún día me gustaría luchar por títulos. Tengo esa ambición, pero tengo 25 años y todavía tengo tiempo", afirmó.

articles.title: Otra fuente de ingresos en el Spotify Camp Nou: 700 millones por la venta de licencias individuales de asientos VIP

articles.summary: Se comercializan 2000 localidades mediante contratos de 15 y 30 años y con un pago inicial
articles.body: El Spotify Camp Nou será, y es, una gran fuente de ingresos para la entidad azulgrana. El Barcelona, de hecho, anunció este viernes que pone a la venta licencias individuales de asientos VIP de larga duración, de la mano de Legends Global, socio estratégico del club culé en el desarrollo y la comercialización de la oferta de hospitality. La previsión inicial de la entidad es generar alrededor de 700 millones de euros de ingresos comprometidos en los próximos 15 y 30 años correspondientes a este stock de 2.000 localidades. Este nuevo modelo de negocio, innovador en el mercado europeo, permite a los clientes disponer en exclusiva de un asiento VIP en el Spotify Camp Nou durante 15 ó 30 años y con un pago inicial. Los compradores dispondrán de una licencia exclusiva sobre una localidad en esta zona privilegiada del estadio durante el período contratado, con nuevas ventajas y servicios asociados. El Barcelona prevé comercializar estos 2.000 asientos en un período aproximado de dos temporadas y media. Con la entrada en vigor de este nuevo modelo, dejará de estar disponible la anterior fórmula de contratación para este stock. Hasta ahora, la entidad había comercializado 5000 asientos VIP en una primera fase. articles.title: Sereias da Vila renew Rafa Andrade's contract
articles.summary: Rafa Andrade will remain with Santos Futebol Clube through 2027! One of the squad’s leaders, the midfielder has signed a new contract with the Sereias da Vil...
articles.body:
Rafa Andrade will remain with Santos Futebol Clube through 2027! One of the squad's leaders, the midfielder has signed a new contract with the Sereias da Vila through December 31, 2027.

"It's a great joy and a huge honor to be able to keep representing this club for another season. I arrived last year at a time of rebuilding, with many challenges, and being part of that process and helping the Sereias return to the top tier of Brazilian football was very special to me. Now, renewing this contract means our story continues. I want to keep working, improving, and giving my best on the pitch to honor this jersey. I have a lot of affection for this team and for everything we are building together," said the No. 88.

In two years, Rafa Andrade has played 38 matches wearing Peixe's shirt and scored six goals, playing a key role in winning the 2025 Brazilian Women's Serie A2 Championship. Now, before thinking about next season, the midfielder wants to help the Sereias in their pursuit of this year's Paulista Women's Championship title. In the state tournament's play-in round, Alvinegro Praiano will face rivals São Paulo, with the first leg on November 18 and the second on November 22.

"The goal is still very much alive! In the Brasileirão, we were left with the bitter feeling of having come up just short, but that also gave us even more desire to achieve something big. Now we are fully focused on the Paulistão. We know our strength, the work we've been doing, and above all the unity of this group. We're going to fight until the very last minute to finish the year with the title and crown everything we've built this season," she concluded.

Born in Sousa, Paraíba, Rafa Andrade is 29 years old and began her career in São Paulo state football, playing for São Bernardo. She has also played for Portuguesa (SP), Foz Cataratas (SC), Kindermann (SC), Napoli (SC), 3B da Amazônia, Tiradentes (CE), Botafogo (PB), Ferroviária, Palmeiras, and Cruzeiro, her most recent club, where she spent three seasons and often wore the captain's armband. In addition, she has also earned call-ups to Brazil's senior and U-20 national teams.

articles.standfirst: Remontó un 3-0 en contra con cuatro goles en 21 minutos
articles.summary: Remontó un 3-0 en contra con cuatro goles en 21 minutos
articles.body: La selección de Curazao ha remontado un 3-0 como visitante y ha propinado a una descontrolada Costa Rica, del entrenador argentino Fernando Batista, una durísima derrota por 3-4 en el comienzo de la Nations League de la CONCACAF. El conjunto 'tico' terminó el primer tiempo en ventaja de 3-0 con los goles de Orlando Sinclar (m.3) y de Carlos Mora (ms.23 y 45), pero en el segundo tiempo Curazao le dio vuelta al marcador con anotaciones de tres futbolistas que estaban en el banquillo: Kenji Gorre en los minutos 62 y 78, Tahith Chong en el 66, y Jordi Paulina en el 83. Costa Rica parecía que encaminaba el partido apenas al minuto 3 cuando el delantero Orlando Sinclair recibió un pase en el área y remató fuerte y cruzado para batir al portero curazoleño Eloy Room y convertir su primer gol con la camiseta de la selección. La Curazao del entrenador neerlandés Dick Advocaat demostró sus buenas cualidades de control y traslado de la pelota y la habilidad y velocidad de sus extremos, pero se topó con una Costa Rica ordenada y sólida en defensa, que cuando tuvo la oportunidad de atacar lo hizo con contundencia. El extremo derecho costarricense Carlos Mora fue una de las principales figuras del equipo en el primer tiempo en el que marcó dos goles. El primero al minuto 23 cuando robó una pelota cerca del área tras un mal pase de un zaguero caribeño, y definió la jugada con un buen remate colocado lejos del alcance del guardameta. Al cierre del primer tiempo volvió a aparecer Mora, jugador del Universitatea Craiova rumano, y con un gran disparo cruzado desde el borde del área anotó el 3-0 que dejaba el partido prácticamente decidido, o al menos eso parecía. En el segundo tiempo Curazo reaccionó rápidamente. Advocaat envió al campo al minuto 57 a Chong, Paulina y Gorre, y entre ellos tres se encargaron de desestabilizar a la zaga costarricense y de fabricar los cuatro goles de la remontada en el estadio Ricardo Saprissa, en San José. Primero fue Chong quien marcó al 62 tras una buena combinación en el área con Paulina, y luego fue Chong al 66 quien anotó un golazo desde fuera del área. Se desdibujó Costa Rica desde el inicio del segundo tiempo ante una Curazao que retomó el fútbol vistoso y alegre que lo llevó a clasificar al Mundial de 2026, el primero en su historia. El descontrol de Costa Rica era total, lo cambios de Batista no cuajaron y el cuadro tico se salvó de encajar el empate porque Obispo falló un cabezazo en el área chica al minuto 75, pero no corrió la misma suerte 3 minutos después cuando Gorré marcó su segundo gol de la noche, a bocajarro, luego de que la pelota se estrellara en el vertical. Con el 3-3 Curazao se lanzó con todo al ataque en busca de la victoria ante una Costa Rica sin ideas ni control y le dio vuelta al marcador con una linda jugada de conjunto que culminó Paulina al recibir un centro en el área chica al 83. Con este resultado, Curazao, Haití y República Dominicana lideran el grupo A con 3 puntos cada uno, mientras que Costa Rica, Nicaragua y Trinidad y Tobago aún no suman. Esta fase de grupos sólo contempla cuatro partidos para cada equipo: dos de visita y dos de local. Los dos primeros lugares clasificarán a los cuartos de final de la Liga de Naciones. 3. Costa Rica: Abraham Madriz; Carlos Barahona, Jeyland Mitchell, Francisco Calvo, Daryl Araya; Sebastián Acuña, Orlando Galo (Aaron Murillo, m.77), Josimar Alcócer (Kenyel Mitchell, m.58), Carlos Mora; Orlando Sinclair (Gerald Taylor, m.58) y Josimar Méndez. Seleccionador: Fernando Batista. 4. Curazao: Eloy Room; Shurandy Sambo, Jurien Gaari, Sherel Floranus, Arjany Martha (Kenji Gorre, m.57); Juninho Bacuna, Livano Comenencia, Armando Obispo, Leandro Bacuna; Jearl Margaritha (Tahith Chong, m.57) y Jurgen Locadia (Jordi Paulina, m.57). Seleccionador: Dick Advocaat. Goles: 1-0, m.3: Sinclair. 2-0, m.23: Mora. 3-0, m.45: Mora. 3-1, m.62: Gorre. 3-2, m.66: Chong. 3-3, m.78: Gorre. 3-4, m.83: Paulina. Árbitro: el guatemalteco Mario Escobar, amonestó al costarrcense Méndez. articles.title: Kai Havertz returning to Arsenal to be assessed after suffering injury for Germany against Netherlands
articles.summary: Kai Havertz suffered an injury in the first half of Germany's 1-1 draw with Netherlands in their Nations League opener on Thursday; Arsenal forward is returning to his club to receive treatment, with the issue understood to be a suspected muscle strain
articles.body:
Havertz pulled up with the issue after a challenge from Quinten Timber in the first half of Thursday's 1-1 draw in Amsterdam and had to be substituted for Younes Ebnoutalib.

The knock is understood to be a minor muscle strain but the forward is leaving the Germany camp to be treated by Arsenal, meaning he will miss the remaining games of the international window.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," said Germany manager Jurgen Klopp, who also lost Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala to a suspected thigh problem on the night.

"I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

Havertz has started six of Arsenal's eight games in all competitions this season, scoring three goals, but his injury, although not thought to be serious, represents the latest in the series of setbacks.

The 27-year-old was limited to only seven Premier League starts last season due to knee and muscle issues. He also missed the final three months of the 2024/25 due to a hamstring tear.

Another spell out would leave Viktor Gyokeres as Arsenal's as only out-and-out striking option, although Mikel Merino has also been used in the role.

Arsenal resume their Premier League campaign at home to Leeds on Saturday October 10.

Havertz and Musiala are being replaced by Florian Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt in Klopp's squad for Germany's next game.

Where does Havertz's injury leave Arsenal?

Arsenal are optimistic that Havertz has avoided a serious injury. They will take further consolation from the fact the issue has occurred early in the international window, leaving more than two weeks of recovery time before they face Leeds.

But the timing of the injury is still uncomfortable given it comes after their failed efforts to add another option up front in the summer. Havertz's injury history, which includes that lengthy lay-off with a hamstring problem in 2025, adds to the concern.

Gyokeres started in Havertz's absence last season, scoring 21 goals in all competitions, but he has had a tough start to the new campaign, only playing 29 Premier League minutes and registering a solitary shot in two starts against Napoli and Ipswich.

The Sweden international's demotion to a peripheral role in the opening weeks of the season follows Arsenal well-documented pursuits of Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Junior. Gyokeres must seize his chance to show he has a place in Mikel Arteta's plans.

Analysis by Jay Bothroyd on Sky Sports News:

Gyokeres's style is very different to Havertz. He wants to run in behind more, he wants to play on the shoulder more and get down the channels between the centre-back and the full-back.

Obviously, Arsenal are going to have to change the way they play in terms of getting on the half-turn and looking for him early, because he does have speed and he is very strong.

He himself, he needs to do better on the part about holding the ball, because that's what Havertz does. Havertz is a platform. There's good link up play with the front three when he plays.

Gyokeres needs to replicate that but I would say to people that maybe Arteta will look at Merino, because Merino has a lot of the same attributes as Havertz in terms of being technically very good, holding the ball, having good vision and making good passes.

In the box, we've also seen him score some important goals. I think Gryokeres will start, but if he's not doing what he should be doing early on, I think Merino will be in there soon.

articles.title: Championship talking points: Swansea's fine start, West Ham's attacking prowess and Burnley misery reviewed
articles.summary: The Sky Sports Essential EFL podcast panel of Billy Sharp and Andy Hinchcliffe review the start of the Championship season, including Swansea City's fine start, West Ham's pursuit of bouncing back and Burnley's plight
articles.body:
Swansea City are the surprise leaders after eight games, while West Ham are in second with Middlesbrough and Wolves not too far behind.

At the other end are Burnley, still without a win and rooted to the bottom of the table on just four points.

On the latest Sky Sports Essential EFL podcast , Billy Sharp and Andy Hinchcliffe look at all the big talking points from the opening part of the Championship season.

Five wins, two draws and just a sole defeat coming at Southampton so far for Vitor Matos' side. Swansea have won admirers for their high-press, energetic style and their ruthlessness at the back - conceding just six goals so far.

Billy Sharp: "Their pressing reminds me a little bit of Marcelo Bielsa's Leeds. They are trying to win the ball back quickly and then attack you.

"They have got belief. They are top of the league and they are scoring goals. They have got a lot of confidence and they have got some kind fixtures coming up, so they will be looking to keep that momentum going."

Andy Hinchcliffe: "They have got the best defence in the league. They have got energy, urgency and they press teams. There is a real physicality to them as well.

"What I like is that they have got a clear identity. They know how they want to play and they are aggressive with and without the ball.

"When you are top of the league, there is an expectation that comes with it. The challenge is maintaining those energy levels because teams are going to come and sit in against you and make it difficult."

West Ham have shown resilience and attacking prowess

It was a tricky start for West Ham as they went winless in their first three. But they went on to win their next four, before battling back at Millwall to earn a 2-2 draw last Saturday.

They are by far and away the top scorers in the Championship, with 22 goals in their first eight games.

Sharp: "West Ham were expected to go straight back up. They have got passionate fans and a lot of attacking power.

"The comeback at Millwall showed a lot of resilience. You look at the players they have got, Jarrod Bowen, Joel Piroe and the attacking players, and there is a lot of quality there.

"The character in that dressing room is important. They have got players who have been there and done it, and they have got enough quality to cause teams problems." Hinchcliffe: "Their defensive ranking is not as good, but you cannot ignore the attacking firepower they have got.

"They have got players who can win you games. Konstantinos Mavropanos has scored four goals as a centre-back, Bowen's leadership, Manor Solomon, Divine Mukasa and Piroe. They have got so much attacking talent.

"If you look at their bench, they can bring players on who would probably start for most teams in the Championship. That gives you a huge advantage over a long season."

Middlesbrough head into the international break in third place, level on points with West Ham.

Will Lankshear has been a standout summer addition, scoring six times so far, but do they have the depth of squad to challenge for the top two again?

Hinchcliffe: "They have invested heavily and they have got some really good players. The money they got for Hayden Hackney and Morgan Rogers has allowed them to build again.

"They have got a new goalkeeper and they have got depth throughout the squad. You look at the players they can bring off the bench and there is a lot of attacking quality.

"It is still a work in progress, but I expect them to be in that mix for the top two."

Sharp: "Lankshear is a big one for them. If he gets 20 goals, that gives Middlesbrough a massive platform.

"They have got a lot of good players and I expect them to be around the play-offs. They have got enough quality to be in that top eight at least.

"But the Championship is stronger this season. Southampton are strong, there are a lot of good teams, but Middlesbrough should be looking at the top eight and the play-offs."

Is Fer Lopez the best player in the Championship?

Wolves have enjoyed a solid start to the campaign, also. They have picked up 14 points, after a 1-0 win over West Brom on Sunday - with Fer Lopez scoring the winner.

The young Spaniard arrived back at Molineux in the summer, and has been exceptional so far this season. Could he lead Wolves back to the Premier League?

Hinchcliffe: "Lopez looks like a Premier League-level player. There is a real quality about him and the way Wolves want to attack.

"Andre gives them that holding midfield role and allows the attacking players to play with more freedom.

"They have got players who can hurt you and there is a lot of quality in that squad."

Sharp: "He is a big player for them. He has got quality and he can make things happen.

"Kieran Trippier gives them experience and leadership, while Andre gives them balance in midfield.

"When you have got those types of players around you, you have got a platform to build from."

Can Sheffield United finish in the top eight?

Just two wins for Sheffield United so far this season. It has been a slow start under Chris Wilder, but Sharp believes his can still have a successful campaign.

Sharp: "They have changed formation three times this season. Not only do you not know the starting XI, you are not quite sure what formation they are going to line up with.

"They have not found consistency. They have got the players and they have got enough strength in the squad, but there are a lot of changes.

"It is disappointing at the minute, but I still think they can get in the top eight. They just need to build a little bit of momentum and have a bit more belief.

"Romelle Donovan needs to be playing. He is a match-winner. He can certainly change a game.

"The expectation is definitely still there. The fans are not happy with the performances on the pitch, but Chris Wilder will find a way to get results."

Could Wrexham's depth work against them?

It was a huge win for Wrexham on Saturday over Southampton, just their second of the season so far in what has been a mixed start to the campaign. It also followed on from a galling 6-0 loss at West Ham the weekend before.

There has been a lot of chopping and changing from Phil Parkinson so far, as he tries to find his best team to compete.

Hinchcliffe: "Wrexham have got an incredible amount of depth. They have virtually got two Championship teams.

"The challenge for Phil Parkinson is keeping everybody happy because there are going to be very good players who are not starting games.

"They have got impact players all over the pitch and that is going to be important over a long Championship season."

Sharp: "Their recruitment has been excellent. They have built a squad where they can change the team and still have quality.

"Kieffer Moore should play when he is fit because of what he gives them. They have got finishers and they have got players who can change games.

"Some of the new signings might need six or eight weeks to settle into the Championship, but once they do, there is a lot of quality there."

Bottom of the Championship, with just four points to show from their first eight games. No wins so far either for Burnley, it has been a disastrous start for Nicky Hayen.

Sharp: "It has been a slow start. They have not won a game yet and they have conceded far too many goals, which if you had said that about Burnley the last two or three seasons, you would have wondered what I was talking about.

"If you are going to concede goals in the Championship, you are not going to win many games. You need a solid platform. They have not found a formula yet to get a clean sheet or even to find a win.

"Losing Zian Flemming was a major blow. He showed his quality in that first game against West Ham. He could have had four or five goals that day and when you lose someone of that quality, he can win you a game on his own."

Hinchcliffe: "The amount of changes is a major issue. They are still trying to work out what their best eleven is and what style of play is best for these players.

"They are not aggressive enough on and off the ball. You cannot sit in your own half and allow teams to knock the ball around in the Championship. You have got to be more aggressive.

"They have conceded the joint-most goals in the Championship. That just cannot happen after eight games."

Derby County only missed out on the play-offs on the final day of last season, but they have got nowhere near that level yet this season. John Eustace's side find themselves in the bottom three, and would be bottom were it not for nicking a late point at Burnley last Saturday.

Hinchcliffe: " I am not particularly surprised when you look at who they are missing. Last season they had Carlton Morris, Patrick Agyemang and Matt Clarke. Those are three players that have to be playing week in and week out if that team is going to be successful.

"When you take three of your very best players out of any Championship team, if you have not got that depth of squad, it is going to be a struggle.

"When you are missing big characters, it does affect a dressing room. It does affect the feeling players go out and play with when some of your main men are not available."

Sharp: "Those are three big players for Derby. It is very unfortunate to lose three players of that quality at the same time.

"If Derby were losing games 1-0 or looking solid, you could say when we get these players back, we will be fine. But they are not really creating a great deal and they are conceding goals as well.

"They cannot just rely on those three players, but I will give them the benefit of the doubt. They are three big players for Derby County."

Faizon Brandon has looked every bit like a top-3 prospect in the Class of 2026—at least so far. The freshman sensation is the first player since Johnny Manziel in 2012 to tally six or more passing touchdowns and three or more rushing touchdowns through his first three career games.

This offense has been dominant with Brandon and a two-headed rushing duo in DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris. Still, it's worth noting they've only faced one FBS opponent this season.

Additionally, Faizon faces significant challenges, as starting freshman quarterbacks have only won 6 out of 49 games against AP No. 1 ranked teams since 2000.

Texas is already battle-tested after defeating then-ranked AP No. 1 Ohio State in Week 2. But Arch Manning has not looked the part of a Heisman Trophy contender. In Week 3, Manning completed just 50 percent of his passes.

Tennessee's defensive line is relentless, limiting opposing quarterbacks to 2.34 seconds per throw, the second-best mark in the nation.

This is going to be a rowdy environment, and I expect the Vols' defense to stymie Manning with their pressure, while Brandon does just enough to pull off an upset.

articles.title: El increíble 1,14 de Haaland: "Es imposible explicarlo"
articles.standfirst: Con su selección, marca más goles que partidos juega. Con el doblete ante Dinamarca, ya suma 64 tantos en 56 encuentros
articles.summary: Con su selección, marca más goles que partidos juega. Con el doblete ante Dinamarca, ya suma 64 tantos en 56 encuentros con Noruega.
articles.body: "Mi especialidad es marcar goles. Simplemente, soy muy bueno marcando y tengo bastante suerte". Sin alardes, con tranquilidad, Haaland pronunciaba estas palabras durante el pasado Mundial después de firmar un doblete ante Senegal. Tenía razón en lo que decía. Sus números anotadores son espectaculares, extraordinarios cuando se pone la camiseta de la selección de Noruega. Erling firmó este jueves otros dos tantos en la victoria de los noruegos contra Dinamarca (3-2) y elevó su cuenta realizadora a 64 dianas en 56 partidos con su combinado nacional. Es decir, marca más goles que partidos juega. El promedio que le sale es de un 'cíborg': 1,14 tantos por encuentro. "Es una locura", dice su compañero Sander Berge. "Después de tantos años viéndolo marcar una y otra vez, uno entiende que está entre los mejores y que sus estadísticas son increíbles. Es impresionante", continúa. "Haaland es, en mi opinión, el mejor futbolista del mundo", dice, por su parte, Kristoffer Ajer. Con los dos tantos ante los daneses, Haaland alcanzó otro récord y se convirtió en el primer jugador en llegar a los 20 goles en la Nations League. Él ya lleva 21. Precisamente, fue en esa competición en la que se estrenó como anotador con Noruega. La aventura de Haaland con la selección comenzó el 5 de septiembre de 2019 contra Malta. En aquel encuentro jugó 66 minutos, pero no marcó. Para celebrar su primer tanto tuvo que esperar un año hasta el 4 de septiembre de 2020 frente a Austria. En el siguiente encuentro contra Irlanda Norte ya firmó un doblete. La máquina de marcar ya estaba en marcha. Haaland, en los últimos seis partidos que ha jugado, ha marcado nueve goles con Noruega. Hizo siete en la Copa del Mundo y el doblete frente a Dinamarca. Stale Solbakken, su seleccionador, está feliz con su rendimiento. "Tiene unas cualidades físicas fantásticas. Además, está mejor que nunca en la fase de creación de juego, pero posee algo que no se puede entrenar. Es imposible explicarlo o aprenderlo. Nació con ese instinto", aseguraba tras el encuentro ante los daneses. La otra cara, la de enfrentarse a Haaland, la vivió Brian Riemer, el seleccionador danés. "Es un delantero que a veces desaparece del partido y ni te das cuenta. Luego le das la más mínima oportunidad y vas perdiendo". A Erling no se le puede conceder ni un metro. Por eso tiene una media de 1,14 goles por encuentro.

articles.title: Sorloth, un calvario sin fin
articles.standfirst: Tras más de un mes y medio de lesión y recaídas, el noruego sigue sin ver la luz, retrasándose su incorporación al grupo durante este parón
articles.summary: Tras más de un mes y medio de lesión y recaídas, el noruego sigue sin ver la luz, retrasándose su incorporación al grupo durante este parón
articles.body: Aunque se antojaba que las tres semanas de parón liguero debían jugar a favor de la recuperación de Sorloth de una vez por todas, el noruego sigue sin ver la luz. Cumplida la primera, el delantero continúa sin dejarse ver por el césped, sumido en un calvario que a día de hoy convierte en algo totalmente incierto determinar la fecha en que pueda volver a ser uno más en el Atlético. Tras más de mes y medio en la enfermería, con una recaída de su lesión y complicaciones derivadas, su reaparición es todo un misterio, sin que pueda asegurarse, ni descartarse, su presencia ante el Alavés una vez que vuelva el fútbol. Cabe recordar que Sorloth ni siquiera ha llegado a trabajar una semana completa junto a sus compañeros desde que disfrutara de las correspondientes tres semanas de vacaciones posteriores al Mundial, constituyendo sus 68 minutos en la derrota frente a Inglaterra en cuartos, el ya lejano 11 de julio, su última aparición en un partido. Superado el sinsabor sufrido con su selección (Noruega caería en la prórroga), Sorloth se incorporó al Atlético el domingo 2 de agosto, ejercitándose en solitario al contar con jornada de descanso los hombres que venían realizando la pretemporada con Simeone. Sin embargo, tras reencontrarse con el cuerpo técnico al día siguiente, en vísperas de que los rojiblancos partieran a Corea del Sur para completar una minigira de cinco días, no tardaría en comenzar su verdadero calvario. Fuera de la lista para Seúl con el propósito de que sumara en El Cerro las pertinentes sesiones físicas de cada inicio de pretemporada junto a Giuliano, Pubill o Grimaldo, Sorloth ya no superaría esa primera semana de trabajo, tal y como confirmaría el parte médico emitido por el club a la vuelta de su periplo por tierras asiáticas. Una contractura muscular que ha acabado derivando en una lesión sin fin. De hecho, pese a que las estimaciones fijaban entre tres y cuatro semanas su plazo de recuperación, su recaída posterior y los nuevos problemas que le impiden avanzar siguen dilatando una vuelta a la que ahora nadie se atreve a marcar una fecha, aunque el objetivo más optimista sigue pasando por que pueda estrenarse frente al Alavés. Así las cosas, aunque aún restan 15 días para que el Atlético retome la competición en Vitoria el próximo 10 de octubre, la presencia de Sorloth dependerá de los entrenamientos que pueda completar con el grupo en esa semana previa y de las sensaciones que experimente. Para entonces serían dos meses ya en el dique seco, lo que le ha llevado a perderse tanto los ocho partidos disputados por los rojiblancos (siete de LaLiga y uno de Champions) como los compromisos con su selección, pero en vista de su lento proceso de recuperación, se prefiere esperar a acontecimientos. Eso sí, si no fuera ante el Alavés, sí debería llegar a tiempo la semana siguiente, para recibir al Manchester United el martes 13.
